PMC319880.scope: The control of araC transcription from the Pc promoter in Escherichia coli: the DNA sites in the ara regulatory region, which proteins occupy them (araC protein, CAP with cyclic AMP, RNA polymerase), and what that occupancy does to Pc activity. Induction of the araBAD operon from PBAD belongs to a sibling pathway and is OFF-PATHWAY here. The DNase protection and dimethyl sulfate methylation assays themselves, and any measurement that concerns araBAD expression only, are also off-pathway or excluded.

source.citation: Lee NL, Gielow WO, Wallace RG. Mechanism of araC autoregulation and the domains of two overlapping promoters, Pc and PBAD, in the L-arabinose regulatory region of Escherichia coli. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA. 1981 Feb;78(2):752-756.

PMC319880.audit: Drafted against text revision r3 (PMC319880.r3.txt) only, reconciling the round-0 and r2 drafts. Sections read in full: header/title block, abstract, introduction, Materials and Methods, Results (DNA-Protein Contact Sites in the ara Regulatory Region; The A Site Is a 'Classical' Operator for the araC Gene; The A Site Is Not Within PBAD), Discussion including the four numbered objections to Ogden et al., acknowledgements, legends of Figs. 1-7, and the reference list (consulted only to see what is cited). This is a transcription-control paper: it reports no metabolite conversion of the requested pathway. Enzymes with a stated catalytic role: RNA polymerase (holoenzyme, 73% and 64% sigma-saturated preparations) - initiates transcription at Pc and at PBAD, the only biosynthetic catalysis in the paper (R1, O1); DNase I - cleaves the DNA backbone, assay reporter only (O3). Dimethyl sulfate is a chemical methylating reagent, not an enzyme (O2). Enzymes/proteins named without any stated reaction: araC protein (P1, P2, and the D-fucose form P1') and CAP/cyclic AMP-binding protein (catabolite gene-activator protein) are sequence-specific DNA-binding regulators, no catalysis stated; the araBAD products are referred to only as 'enzymes required for the metabolism of L-arabinose' with no individual reaction (S1); the restriction enzymes HpaII, BamHI, Sau96AI, HhaI, HaeII, HaeIII and MboII appear only as fragment-generating tools in Fig. 1 and the figure legends, with no reaction stated. Numerical landmarks the paper fixes: araBAD start +1, araC start -148, 147-bp nontranscribed region, A site/polymerase site in Pc -105 to -170 (competition region -105 to -147), high-affinity CAP site -77 to -110, B site -42 to -80, low-affinity CAP site -130 to -140, PBAD polymerase protection -39 to at least +24. Text-revision note: r3 restores the body of the article as continuous prose, so quotes are taken from the abstract, Results and Discussion in preference to figure legends. Two spans still carry transposed words where lines cross the page-3 figure regions (the 250 microM cAMP protection sentence, and the D-fucose/P1' conformation sentence); both are skipped rather than quoted.
